<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<example_2>

5 0 5

</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Recolor every non-zero cell to 5; zeros stay 0.
output(R, C, 5) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0.
output(R, C, 0) :- input(R, C, 0).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_2>

<grid_1>

</diagram>

</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, Cin, Color), n_cols(M), C = M - 1 - Cin.

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_3>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Exactly one output per cell
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Define two non-zero cells
nonzero(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,Color), Color != 0.

% Pick the two cells (must be the only two)
cell1(R1,C1,Col1) :- nonzero(R1,C1,Col1).
cell2(R2,C2,Col2) :- nonzero(R2,C2,Col2), Col2 != Col1.

% Period for horizontal stripes (rows equal)
horiz :- R1 = R2.
% Period for vertical stripes (columns equal)
vert :- C1 = C2.

% Ensure exactly one orientation is true
:- not horiz, not vert.
:- horiz, vert.

% Ordering constraints to avoid ambiguity
:- horiz, C2 <= C1.   % ensure C2 > C1 when horizontal
:- vert, R2 <= R1.    % ensure R2 > R1 when vertical

% Horizontal orientation: columns vary
period_h := 2 * (C2 - C1).

output(R,C,Col1) :- horiz, (C % period_h = C1 % period_h).
output(R,C,Col2) :- horiz, (C % period_h = C2 % period_h).
output(R,C,0) := horiz, not (C % period_h = C1 % period_h), not (C % period_h = C2 % period_h).

% Vertical orientation: rows vary
period_v := 2 * (R2 - R1).

output(R,C,Col1) :- vert, (R % period_v = R1 % period_v).
output(R,C,Col2) :- vert, (R % period_v = R2 % period_v).
output(R,C,0) := vert, not (R % period_v = R1 % period_v), not (R % period_v = R2 % period_v).

% Forbid any other color on any cell
:- output(R,C,X), X != Col1, X != Col2, X != 0.

% Exactly one color per output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Show the result
#show output/3.
</asp>

% Define grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output cell predicate
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Non‑zero cells in the input
nonzero(R,C,Col) :- input(R,C,Col), Col != 0.

% Choose the two coloured cells (must be the only two non‑zero cells)
cell1(R1,C1,Col1) :- nonzero(R1,C1,Col1).
cell2(R2,C2,Col2) :- nonzero(R2,C2,Col2), Col2 != Col1.

% Orientation: rows equal -> horizontal strips; columns equal -> vertical strips
horiz :- R1 = R2.
vert  :- C1 = C2.

% Exactly one of the two orientations must hold and they cannot both hold
:- not horiz, not vert.   % at least one true
:- horiz, vert.           % not both true

% Ensure the “right” cell is really to the right / below the “left” cell
% (prevents swapping the two cells)
:- horiz, C2 <= C1.
:- vert,  R2 <= R1.

% Period for the two possible orientations
period_h := 2 * (C2 - C1).    % used only when horiz is true
period_v := 2 * (R2 - R1).    % used only when vert  is true

% -------- Horizontal case (rows equal) --------
output(R,C,Col1) :- horiz, (C % period_h = C1 % period_h).
output(R,C,Col2) :- horiz, (C % period_h = C2 % period_h).
output(R,C,0)    :- horiz, not (C % period_h = C1 % period_h), not (C % period_h = C2 % period_h).

% -------- Vertical case (columns equal) --------
output(R,C,Col1) :- vert,  (R % period_v = R1 % period_v).
output(R,C,Col2) :- vert,  (R % period_v = R2 % period_v).
output(R,C,0)    :- vert,  not (R % period_v = R1 % period_v), not (R % period_v = R2 % period_v).

% Forbid any colour other than the two given colours or 0 on any cell
:- output(R,C,X), X != Col1, X != Col2, X != 0.

% Exactly one colour per output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

#show output/3.
</asp>

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(Nr) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(Nc) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..Nr-1) :- n_rows(Nr).
col(0..Nc-1) :- n_cols(Nc).
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Choose a pair of cells with distinct colors
pair(R1,C1,R2,C2,Col1,Col2) :-
    (horizontal_pair(R1,C1,C2,Col1,Col2,R2) ; vertical_pair(R1,R2,C1,Col1,Col2)).

horizontal_pair(R1,C1,C2,Col1,Col2,R2) :-
    input(R1,C1,Col1), input(R2,C2,Col2),
    Col1 != Col2, Col1 != 0, Col2 != 0,
    C1 < C2.

vertical_pair(R1,R2,C,Col1,Col2) :-
    input(R1,C,Col1), input(R2,C,Col2),
    Col1 != Col2, Col1 != 0, Col2 != 0,
    R1 < R2,
    C = C.

% Periods
horiz_period(P) :- pair(R1,C1,R2,C2,Col1,Col2), C1 < C2, P = 2 * (C2 - C1).
vert_period(P) :- pair(R1,C1,R2,C2,Col1,Col2), C1 = C2, R1 < R2, P = 2 * (R2 - R1).

% Output pattern
output(R,C,Col1) :- horiz_period(P), mod(C, P, C1).
output(R,C,Col2) :- horiz_period(P), mod(C, P, C2).
output(R,C,0) :- horiz_period(P), not mod(C, P, C1), not mod(C, P, C2).

output(R,C,Col1) :- vert_period(P), mod(R, P, R1).
output(R,C,Col2) :- vert_period(P), mod(R, P, R2).
output(R,C,0) :- vert_period(P), not mod(R, P, R1), not mod(R, P, R2).

% Exactly one color per output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% No other colors (optional)

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output cell predicate
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Non‑zero cells in the input
nonzero(R,C,Col) :- input(R,C,Col), Col != 0.

% Choose the two coloured cells (must be the only two non‑zero cells)
cell1(R1,C1,Col1) :- nonzero(R1,C1,Col1).
cell2(R2,C2,Col2) :- nonzero(R2,C2,Col2), Col2 != Col1.

% Orientation: rows equal -> horizontal strips; columns equal -> vertical strips
horiz :- R1 = R2.
vert  :- C1 = C2.

% Exactly one of the two orientations must hold and they cannot both hold
:- not horiz, not vert.   % at least one true
:- horiz, vert.           % not both true

% Ensure the “right” cell is really to the right / below the “left” cell
% (prevents swapping the two cells)
:- horiz, C2 <= C1.
:- vert,  R2 <= R1.

% Period for the two possible orientations
period_h := 2 * (C2 - C1).    % used only when horiz is true
period_v := 2 * (R2 - R1).    % used only when vert  is true

% -------- Horizontal case (rows equal) --------
output(R,C,Col1) :- horiz, (C % period_h = C1 % period_h).
output(R,C,Col2) :- horiz, (C % period_h = C2 % period_h).
output(R,C,0)    :- horiz, not (C % period_h = C1 % period_h), not (C % period_h = C2 % period_h).

1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly two coloured cells (non‑zero) must appear in the input
#count{ R,C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0 } = 2.

% Choose the two coloured cells (order them so that C1 ≤ C2 and R1 ≤ R2)
pair(R1,C1,R2,C2,V1,V2) :-
    input(R1,C1,V1), V1 != 0,
    input(R2,C2,V2), V2 != 0,
    C1 <= C2,
    R1 <= R2.

% Orientation predicates
horiz :- R1 = R2.                     % same row  → horizontal pattern
vert  :- C1 = C2.                     % same column → vertical pattern

% Flags that decide which period to use
use_h :- horiz.                     % horizontal pattern (also for diagonal case)
use_h :- not horiz, not vert.      % diagonal case is treated as horizontal
use_v :- vert.                      % vertical pattern

% Periods for the two orientations
period_h(P) :- use_h, C1 < C2, P = 2 * (C2 - C1).
period_v(P) :- use_v, R1 < R2, P = 2 * (R2 - R1).

% Helper predicates for the positions where the two colours appear
col_of_V1(C) :- period_h(P), C = C1 + K * P, K >= 0.
col_of_V2(C) :- period_h(P), C = C2 + K * P, K >= 0.
row_of_V1(R) :- period_v(P), R = R1 + K * P, K >= 0.
row_of_V2(R) :- period_v(P), R = R2 + K * P, K >= 0.

% Horizontal (including diagonal) case
output(R,C,V1) :- period_h(P), col_of_V1(C).
output(R,C,V2) :- period_h(P), col_of_V2(C).
output(R,C,0)   :- period_h(P), not col_of_V1(C), not col_of_V2(C).

% Vertical case
output(R,C,V1) :- period_v(P), row_of_V1(R).
output(R,C,V2) :- period_v(P), row_of_V2(R).
output(R,C,0)   :- period_v(P), not row_of_V1(R), not row_of_V2(R).

% Exactly one colour per cell
1 { output(R,C,Col) : color(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% No other colours besides the two given ones and 0 may appear
:- output(R,C,X), X != V1, X != V2, X != 0.

#show output/3.
</asp>
